item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 291126
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, near the Baja California Peninsula of Mexico, on Hurricane
Nolo, located several hundred miles west of Honolulu, Hawaii, and on
Tropical Storm Rachel, located few hundred miles south-southwest of
Lazaro Cardenas, Mexico.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (EP91):
An area of low pressure located well east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands is producing limited showers and thunderstorms this morning.
Only a slight increase in shower and thunderstorm organization is
needed for it to become a tropical depression during the next day or
two while it moves slowly east-northeastward. Environmental
conditions are expected to become less conducive for development
late this week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Polo Public Advisory Number 36
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 291443
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Advisory Number  36
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 AM MST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
...POLO ABOUT TO MAKE LANDFALL NEAR GUAYMAS MEXICO...
...CONDITIONS DETERIORATING IN THE LANDFALL AREA...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...27.8N 110.9W
ABOUT 15 MI...20 KM S OF GUAYMAS MEXICO
ABOUT 130 MI...205 KM NNE OF LORETO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...75 MPH...120 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NE OR 40 DEGREES AT 17 MPH...28 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...981 MB...28.97 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The Government of Mexico has discontinued all warnings for the west 
coast of Baja California Sur. The Government of Mexico has changed 
the Hurricane Warning to a Tropical Storm Warning for the east 
coast of Baja California Sur from Loreto to Santa Rosalia, and has 
discontinued all other watches and warnings on the east coast of 
Baja California Sur.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Mainland Mexico from Bahia Kino to Huatabampito
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Mainland Mexico south of Huatabampito to Topolobampo
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* East coast of Baja California Sur from Loreto to Santa Rosalia
* Mainland Mexico south of Huatabampito to Topolobampo
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area, in this case in the next few 
hours
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area, in this case in the next several hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area.
 
Interests in the remainder of Sonora and northern Sinaloa should
monitor the progress of Polo.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Polo was located
near latitude 27.8 North, longitude 110.9 West. Polo is moving
toward the northeast near 17 mph (28 km/h) and this motion is
expected to continue with an increase in forward speed today. On 
the forecast track, the core of Polo will move inland over southern 
Sonora near Guaymas during the next few hours and cross portions of 
northwestern Mexico this afternoon.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 75 mph (120 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Little change in strength is expected before landfall. 
Rapid weakening is expected after landfall as the center crosses 
northwestern Mexico.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles
(150 km). The Mexican Navy automated station in Guaymas recently 
reported a wind gust of 52 mph (84 km/h).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 981 mb (28.97 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area and
possible in the watch area during the next few hours. Hurricane and 
tropical storm conditions are expected over northwestern Mexico 
near the center of Polo this afternoon.
 
A Wind Advisory is in effect for portions of southern New Mexico and
far western Texas where strong gusty winds are possible late today
and tonight in association with Polo’s remnants. Refer to products
issued by your local National Weather Service Forecast Office for
additional information.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 6 
inches across southern and central portions of Sonora with isolated 
maximum totals of 8 inches. An additional 1 to 2 inches of rainfall 
is expected across Baja California Sur. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo, 
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic 
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURGE: A storm surge is expected to produce significant coastal
flooding in areas of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will
be accompanied by large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will continue to affect portions of
the coast of the Baja California peninsula and northwestern Mexico
during the next day or so. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1100 AM MST.
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 36
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Tue Sep 29 2026 
432 
WTPZ42 KNHC 291444
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  36
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 AM MST Tue Sep 29 2026

Polo is now over the Gulf of California, with convection increasing 
near the center. The cyclone weakened during its passage over Baja 
California del Sur, but the consensus of the satellite intensity 
estimates is that it remains a hurricane with winds near 65 kt.

The initial motion is now 040/15. Polo is expected to accelerate 
northeastward in the flow on the east side of a mid-latitude trough 
over the southwestern United States.  The forecast track shows the 
cyclone making landfall near Guaymas in the next few hours and then 
crossing northwestern Mexico until dissipation occurs.

Little change in strength is likely before landfall. After landfall 
the surface circulation should weaken rapidly over the rough terrain 
of northwestern Mexico, with the circulation dissipating between 
12-24 h. However, Polo's remnant vorticity will continue moving 
northeastward and likely interact and phase with aforementioned 
mid-latitude trough digging into the Four Corners region of the U.S. 
on Tuesday night and Wednesday.  This will contribute to heavy 
rainfall, flash flooding, and gusty winds in the southwestern U.S. 
and southern Plains. See products issued by the Weather Prediction 
Center and local National Weather Service offices for more 
information.
  
Key Messages:
 
1. Hurricane conditions are expected in southern Sonora as the 
center of Polo moves inland, and residents there should remain in a 
safe shelter through this morning. Hurricane and tropical storm 
conditions will spread across northwestern Mexico near the center 
of Polo through this afternoon. A dangerous storm surge is expected 
at the coast in areas of onshore winds.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact the southern and 
central portions of Sonora today. This rainfall is expected to 
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas 
of steep terrain. Moisture from Polo will support heavy rainfall and 
flooding potential across the Southwest U.S. into the Southern High 
Plains today into early Wednesday.
 
3. Even after Polo dissipates, its low- to mid-level remnants may 
produce strong gusty winds well inland over the higher terrain of 
northwest Mexico, southern New Mexico, and far western Texas.
 
4. Dangerous surf and rip currents are likely along portions of the
northwest coast of Mexico and Baja California for the next day or
so.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  29/1500Z 27.8N 110.9W   65 KT  75 MPH
 12H  30/0000Z 30.5N 108.2W   40 KT  45 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 24H  30/1200Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.description:

PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Coast of southwestern Mexico from Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Coast of southwestern Mexico north of Playa Perula to Cabo
Corrientes
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM CST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was
located near latitude 15.3 North, longitude 105.0 West. Rachel is
moving toward the west-northwest near 13 mph (20 km/h). A general
northwestward motion at a slower forward speed is expected during
the next few days. On the forecast track, the center of Rachel is
predicted to move parallel to, but stay offshore of, the coast of
southwestern Mexico.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts. Gradual strengthening is expected during the next few days, 
and Rachel is forecast to become a hurricane later today. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 160 miles (260 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 987 mb (29.15 inches).

----------------------

Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected in the warning area 
later today or tonight. Tropical storm conditions are possible in 
the watch area by tonight or Wednesday.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8 
inches, with isolated maximum totals of 12 inches across coastal 
portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero, Michoacán, Colima and 
Jalisco. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and 
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will affect portions of the
southwestern coast of Mexico during the next couple of days and
spread northward through the end of the week. These swells are
likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1200 PM CST.
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 291452
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
900 AM CST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
Rachel is dealing with around 20 kt of northeasterly wind shear this 
morning, with the estimated center position located along the far 
northern edge of the central dense overcast. However, a burst of 
deep convection, with cloud top temperatures of around -90 C, along 
with strong upper-level outflow suggests that the system is slowly 
intensifying. The latest TAFB Dvorak intensity estimate was 3.5/55 
kt, while recent objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range 
from 43-55 kt. Given the deepening convection and the slight 
increase in intensity estimates, the initial intensity is set at 55 
kt for this advisory. 
 
The strong tropical storm is moving toward the west-northwest around 
11 kt, steered by a strong mid-level ridge centered over the 
south-central United States. A turn toward the northwest is expected 
later today as high pressure builds over eastern Mexico, followed by 
a gradual decrease in forward speed as Rachel moves into a region 
with weaker steering flow. By late week, building high pressure to 
the northwest of the cyclone should induce a gradual turn back 
toward the west-northwest and then west, accompanied by a slight 
increase in forward speed. The updated forecast track is very 
similar to the previous advisory, remaining near the middle of the 
track forecast guidance envelope through 48 h and near the northern 
end of the guidance thereafter. 
 
Decreasing wind shear, sufficiently warm sea surface temperatures 
and favorable upper-level divergence are expected to support 
strengthening over the next couple of days, and Rachel is forecast 
to become a hurricane later today. However, Rachel could briefly 
move over slightly cooler waters left in the wake of Hurricane Polo 
tonight into early Wednesday, which may temporarily limit the rate 
of intensification. Thereafter, warmer waters should support 
additional strengthening through late this week. The latest NHC 
intensity forecast is near the upper-end of the guidance envelope, 
although it remains slightly below the HCCA solution. 
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Although the core of Rachel is forecast to remain offshore of 
Mexico, tropical-storm-force winds are expected along a portion of 
the coast of southwestern Mexico in the Tropical Storm Warning area 
today or tonight. Tropical storm conditions are possible in the 
watch area tonight or on Wednesday.
 
2. Outer bands from Rachel will bring locally heavy rainfall to
portions of coastal southwest Mexico through Thursday. This rainfall
may produce areas of flooding and mudslides, especially in regions
of steep terrain.
 
3. Large waves could produce life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions along portions of the southwestern coast of Mexico during
the next several days.

BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Advisory Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP192026
800 AM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026
 
...NEW TROPICAL DEPRESSION EXPECTED TO BE SHORT-LIVED WELL OFFSHORE
OF MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.4N 131.6W
ABOUT 1535 MI...2470 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...E OR 90 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Nineteen-E was located near latitude 14.4 North, longitude 131.6
West. The depression is moving toward the east near 9 mph (15 km/h)
and this motion is expected to continue for the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
The depression could become a tropical storm later today before 
weakening on Wednesday.  The system is likely to degenerate into a 
post-tropical cyclone by late Thursday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.

Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 291451
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP192026
800 AM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026

Satellite images indicate that the system well west-southwest of 
Baja California Sur (former Invest EP91) has had enough organized 
deep convection with a well-defined circulation to be considered a 
tropical depression.  The initial intensity is set to 30 kt, 
consistent with an overnight scatterometer pass and a Dvorak 2.0 
from TAFB.  

Although the system has become a tropical depression, the center is 
mostly exposed with moderate shear.  There is a slight chance of the 
system reaching tropical storm intensity later today before it feels 
the cold wake of former Hurricane Odalys by tomorrow.  The 
environment is expected to further dry out during the next couple of 
days with an increase in shear.  These factors should cause the 
depression to weaken by late Wednesday and degenerate into a post- 
tropical cyclone by late Thursday.  The NHC forecast is just above 
the model consensus.

The depression is moving eastward at 8 kt.  This general motion is 
expected for the next few days until dissipation while the cyclone 
remains embedded in westerly flow due to a northward-displaced 
near-equatorial trough, enhanced by both the strong El Nino event 
and western Hemisphere Madden-Julian Oscillation.  The track is 
close to a blend of the ECMWF and GFS models and leans toward the 
HCCA corrected-consensus model.
